court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Sairaj Bhanudas Gade And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sairaj S/O Bhanudas Gade and others (husband, wife, etc.)
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Maharashtra and another

facts_of_case: Parties arrived at an amicable settlement to end marital ties. Husband filed a petition for divorce in Family Court, Aurangabad. Parties agreed on terms including permanent alimony.

legal_principles.principle: The power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences.
legal_principles.held: The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus: The power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2007) 4 CTC 769
Sairaj Bhanudas Gade And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 12 April, 2022
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in quashing criminal proceedings

legal_principles.principle: Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.
legal_principles.held: Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2007) 4 CTC 769
Sairaj Bhanudas Gade And Others vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 12 April, 2022
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — significance in quashing criminal proceedings

outcome.final_order: Quashing of FIR and proceedings sought and granted.
